findings.motion: HB 259 Election Integrity Act, Second Reading (vote 61-48)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on second reading. The committee substitute codifies a citizenship requirement to vote and sets up checks of voter registration and citizenship status against jury-excusal and federal records.

findings.motion: SB 747 Elections Law Changes, Second Reading (vote 69-47)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on second reading. The act (SL 2023-140) includes same-day registration that requires photo identification plus a proof-of-residence document, and keeps photo ID as a ground to challenge a voter at the polls. The history also shows Aye on many floor amendments to this bill that failed; their contents were not read.

findings.motion: SB 747 Elections Law Changes, Veto Override (vote 72-44)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on the vote to override the veto of SB 747.

findings.motion: HB 1074 Constitutional Amendment/Citizens-Only Voting, Second Reading (vote 104-12)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on second reading of the proposed constitutional amendment that only a citizen of the United States may vote. The same history shows Aye on an amendment (A1 Harrison) that failed 46-70. The history shows a different entry on third reading (next record).

findings.motion: HB 1074 Constitutional Amendment/Citizens-Only Voting, Third Reading (vote 99-12)
findings.note: Member vote history shows Aye on third reading of HB 1074 (SL 2024-18), the proposed constitutional amendment limiting voting to citizens.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (vote 66-47)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on second reading. The ratified bill requires a voter registration application to state that the applicant is a citizen, with a notice and a statement under penalty of perjury if the answer is blank, and sets monthly sharing of motor-vehicle records for voter-roll maintenance.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (vote 62-47)
findings.note: Member vote history shows No on the concurrence vote; the bill page shows a Governor's veto of House Bill 958.

findings.motion: House second reading, HB 958 Election Law Changes (RCS H-758, 66 to 47)
findings.note: Voted No on second reading in the House. Roll call shown on the official bill page. HB 958, Election Law Changes (2025-26 session). Per the official bill digest it, among other things: requires a statement of US citizenship (under penalty of perjury) on voter registration applications; requires covered military and overseas voters to send a copy of the photo ID used for in-person voting with the ballot; and extends the deadline for a voter to show ID after a provisional ballot to noon on the fifth business day after the election. It was ratified 2026-08-06 and vetoed by the Governor 2026-08-17.

It was ratified 2026-08-06 and vetoed by the Governor 2026-08-17.
